lessons.title: Hedging and guessing
lessons.goal: Express opinions cautiously and make educated guesses instead of speaking in black and white.

tip.title: Soften, then guess
tip.body: To hedge an opinion, frame it: Yo diría que… (I'd say), Me da la impresión de que… (I get the impression that), Hasta cierto punto (up to a point), A lo mejor me equivoco, pero… (I may be wrong, but). Puede que takes the subjunctive: Puede que tengan razón. To guess about the present, Spanish uses the future tense: Estará en una reunión = he's probably in a meeting. Deber de + infinitive also expresses a supposition (Debe de tener cuarenta años), although in everyday speech many people drop the de. For "maybe", Spain also says igual, Mexico igual y… and Argentina capaz que…

phrases.t: Yo diría que es una buena idea, aunque con matices.
phrases.n: I'd say it's a good idea, though with some reservations.

phrases.t: Me da la impresión de que no lo tienen nada claro.
phrases.n: I get the impression they're not at all clear about it.

phrases.t: A lo mejor me equivoco, pero creo que se están precipitando.
phrases.n: I may be wrong, but I think they're rushing into it.
phrases.note: Spain also: Igual me equivoco…; Argentina: Capaz que me equivoco…

phrases.t: Hasta cierto punto, tienes razón.
phrases.n: Up to a point, you're right.

phrases.t: Puede que tengan razón, pero lo dudo.
phrases.n: They may be right, but I doubt it.

phrases.t: Estará en una reunión.
phrases.n: He's probably in a meeting.
phrases.note: Future of probability: a guess about the present.

phrases.t: Debe de tener unos cuarenta años.
phrases.n: She must be about forty.
phrases.note: deber de + infinitive = supposition; in speech often debe tener.

phrases.t: No lo tengo del todo claro.
phrases.n: I'm not entirely sure about it.

lines.name: Dalia
lines.t: ¿Ya viste el plan del nuevo director? Quiere cambiar todo el sistema en un mes.
lines.n: Have you seen the new director's plan yet? He wants to change the whole system in a month.

lines.t: Sí, ya lo vi. Yo diría que la idea es buena, aunque con matices.
lines.n: Yes, I've seen it. I'd say the idea is good, though with some reservations.

lines.name: Dalia
lines.t: ¿Con matices? A mí me parece una locura. ¿Y por qué no vino hoy a la junta?
lines.n: With reservations? It seems crazy to me. And why didn't he come to the meeting today?

lines.t: No sé, estará en otra reunión. Pero me da la impresión de que no lo tienen nada claro.
lines.n: I don't know, he's probably in another meeting. But I get the impression they're not at all clear about it.

lines.name: Dalia
lines.t: ¿Tú crees que lo van a aplicar así, tal cual?
lines.n: Do you think they're going to implement it just like that?

lines.t: Puede que sí, pero lo dudo. A lo mejor me equivoco, pero creo que se están precipitando.
lines.n: They may, but I doubt it. I may be wrong, but I think they're rushing into it.

lessons.title: Ways of becoming
lessons.goal: Choose the right verb for "to become": ponerse, volverse, hacerse, quedarse, llegar a ser, convertirse en.

tip.title: Six ways to change
tip.body: English says "become" or "get"; Spanish chooses by the kind of change. Ponerse + adjective: a sudden, usually temporary change of mood, colour or state (se puso rojo, me puse nervioso). Volverse: a deeper, lasting change of character, often unexpected (se ha vuelto muy desconfiado). Hacerse: a change you work for, or a change of profession, belief or status (se hizo médica, se hizo rico). Quedarse: the state that results from an event, often a loss (se quedó ciego, me quedé sin palabras). Llegar a ser: reaching a goal after a long process. Convertirse en + noun: a transformation (se convirtió en un referente).

phrases.t: Se puso rojo cuando lo felicitaron.
phrases.n: He went red when they congratulated him.

phrases.t: Me puse de muy mal humor.
phrases.n: I got into a really bad mood.

phrases.t: Con los años se ha vuelto más tolerante.
phrases.n: Over the years he's become more tolerant.

phrases.t: Se hizo médica después de años de esfuerzo.
phrases.n: She became a doctor after years of hard work.
phrases.note: hacerse: change through effort. For a man: médico.

phrases.t: Se quedó sin palabras.
phrases.n: She was left speechless.
phrases.note: quedarse: resulting state after an event.

phrases.t: Me quedé de piedra.
phrases.n: I was stunned.

phrases.t: Llegó a ser directora del hospital.
phrases.n: She eventually became director of the hospital.
phrases.note: llegar a ser: the culmination of a long process.

phrases.t: Se convirtió en un referente del sector.
phrases.n: He became a benchmark in the industry.

lessons.title: Indicative or subjunctive: a change of meaning
lessons.goal: Use the mood to change what a sentence means: report or request, a real or any person, information or sympathy, cause or warning.

tip.title: Same words, different message
tip.body: At C1 the mood is a tool for meaning. Decir que + indicative reports information (Le dije que venía = I told him I was coming); + subjunctive it becomes a request (Le dije que viniera = I told him to come). Alguien que + subjunctive is anyone, maybe nobody (Buscamos a alguien que hable japonés); + indicative it's a specific, real person (Conozco a alguien que habla japonés). Entender que + indicative = to gather (Entiendo que no puedes venir); + subjunctive = to sympathise (Entiendo que estés molesto). Como at the start of a sentence + indicative means "since"; + subjunctive it means "if" and sounds like a warning: Como llegues tarde, me voy.

phrases.n: We're looking for someone who speaks Japanese.

lines.name: Valeria
lines.t: Che, te dije que me mandaras el informe antes del mediodía y ya son las tres.

lessons.title: Aspect that changes meaning
lessons.goal: Use the preterite and imperfect of conocer, saber, querer, poder and tener que to say exactly what happened.

tip.title: Preterite = event, imperfect = background
tip.body: With some verbs the choice between preterite and imperfect changes the English translation. Conocía = I knew; conocí = I met. Sabía = I knew; supe = I found out. Quería = I wanted; quise = I tried; no quise = I refused. Podía = I was able (in general); pude = I managed; no pude = I tried and failed. Tenía que = I was supposed to (did I? unclear); tuve que = I had to, and I did. Iba a + infinitive = I was going to, which often implies it didn't happen: Iba a llamarte, pero…

lessons.title: Does remote work isolate us?
lessons.goal: Follow a radio interview full of careful, hedged statements.

phrases.t: Yo no me atrevería a afirmarlo.
phrases.n: I wouldn't go so far as to say that.

phrases.t: Todo apunta a que depende de cada persona.
phrases.n: Everything suggests it depends on the individual.

phrases.t: Habría que matizarlo.
phrases.n: That would need some qualification.

phrases.t: No está del todo claro que sea así.
phrases.n: It's not entirely clear that that's the case.

story.title: ¿Nos aísla el teletrabajo?
story.intro: On a Spanish radio programme, a presenter interviews a Mexican sociologist about remote work and loneliness.

lines.name: Inés
lines.t: Buenas tardes. Hoy hablamos con el sociólogo mexicano Andrés Ramírez. Profesor, ¿el teletrabajo nos está haciendo más solitarios?
lines.n: Good afternoon. Today we're talking to the Mexican sociologist Andrés Ramírez. Professor, is remote work making us lonelier?

lines.name: Andrés
lines.t: Bueno, yo no me atrevería a afirmarlo de una forma tan tajante. Todo apunta a que depende mucho de cada persona.
lines.n: Well, I wouldn't go so far as to say it so categorically. Everything suggests it depends a lot on the individual.

lines.name: Inés
lines.t: ¿En qué sentido?
lines.n: In what sense?

lines.name: Andrés
lines.t: Por un lado, hay quien se siente más libre y pasa más tiempo con su familia. Por otro, puede que quienes viven solos extrañen el contacto diario con los compañeros.
lines.n: On the one hand, some people feel freer and spend more time with their family. On the other, those who live alone may miss daily contact with colleagues.
lines.note: extrañar = to miss (Latin America); Spain usually: echar de menos.

lines.name: Inés
lines.t: Se dice que la soledad ha aumentado muchísimo en los últimos años. ¿Lo confirma?
lines.n: People say loneliness has increased enormously in recent years. Do you confirm that?

lines.name: Andrés
lines.t: Habría que matizarlo. Es cierto que se habla mucho de soledad, pero no está del todo claro que la causa sea el teletrabajo.
lines.n: That would need some qualification. It's true that there's a lot of talk about loneliness, but it's not entirely clear that remote work is the cause.

lines.name: Inés
lines.t: Entonces, ¿qué recomendaría usted?
lines.n: So what would you recommend?

lines.name: Andrés
lines.t: Yo diría que lo ideal es combinar: trabajar desde casa unos días e ir a la oficina uno o dos días por semana, aunque solo sea para tomar un café con los compañeros.
lines.n: I'd say the ideal is to combine the two: work from home some days and go to the office one or two days a week, even if it's only to have a coffee with colleagues.

lessons.title: Press interview
lessons.goal: Answer a journalist's tough questions without confirming rumours. Your choices shape the story.

phrases.t: Por ahora no puedo confirmar ni desmentir esa información.
phrases.n: For now I can neither confirm nor deny that information.

phrases.t: Yo no me atrevería a dar cifras.
phrases.n: I wouldn't venture to give any figures.

phrases.t: No es que lo niegue, es que todavía no hay nada decidido.
phrases.n: It's not that I'm denying it, it's that nothing has been decided yet.

phrases.t: Entiendo que estén preocupados.
phrases.n: I understand that they're worried.

branch.title: Rumores de cierre
branch.scene: You're the spokesperson for a manufacturing company in Colombia. Outside the head office in Bogotá, a radio journalist asks you about rumours that the company's plant in Cali will close.
branch.name: Catalina Ríos

start.t: Buenos días. Se rumorea que la empresa va a cerrar la planta de Cali. ¿Lo confirma?
start.n: Good morning. There are rumours that the company is going to close the Cali plant. Do you confirm it?

choices.t: Buenos días. Por ahora no puedo confirmar ni desmentir esa información.
choices.n: Good morning. For now I can neither confirm nor deny that information.

choices.t: Sí, es verdad: cerramos en marzo.
choices.n: Yes, it's true: we're closing in March.

cautious.t: Pero según algunas fuentes, habría más de doscientos despidos.
cautious.n: But according to some sources, there could be more than two hundred redundancies.

choices.t: Yo no me atrevería a dar cifras. Lo que sí puedo decirle es que estamos estudiando varias opciones.
choices.n: I wouldn't venture to give any figures. What I can tell you is that we're looking at several options.

choices.t: ¡Eso es mentira! ¿Quién le ha dicho eso?
choices.n: That's a lie! Who told you that?

choices.t: Perdone, me he expresado mal. No es que lo niegue, es que todavía no hay nada decidido.
choices.n: Sorry, I expressed myself badly. It's not that I'm denying it, it's that nothing has been decided yet.

choices.t: No tengo nada más que decir.
choices.n: I have nothing more to say.

options.t: ¿Y cuáles son esas opciones? Los trabajadores están muy preocupados.
options.n: And what are those options? The workers are very worried.

choices.t: Entiendo que estén preocupados. Le garantizo que hablaremos con ellos antes de tomar cualquier decisión.
choices.n: I understand that they're worried. I can assure you we'll talk to them before making any decision.

choices.t: Es posible que se traslade parte de la producción, pero no está decidido.
choices.n: Part of production may be moved, but it hasn't been decided.

follow.t: O sea, ¿que podría haber traslados a otra ciudad?
follow.n: So there could be transfers to another city?

choices.t: Podría ser una opción, pero insisto: no hay nada decidido, y los trabajadores serán los primeros en saberlo.
choices.n: It could be one option, but I insist: nothing has been decided, and the workers will be the first to know.

choices.t: Bueno, sí, más o menos. Pero eso no lo publique.
choices.n: Well, yes, more or less. But don't publish that.

good.t: Muy bien, así lo contaré. Gracias por su tiempo.
good.n: Very well, that's how I'll report it. Thank you for your time.
good.outcome: You stayed precise and hedged, showed empathy and gave the journalist nothing to misquote.

bad.t: Muchas gracias. Ya tengo mi titular.
bad.n: Thank you very much. I've got my headline.
bad.outcome: You confirmed the rumour or lost your temper, and the story will run without your side. Hedge with no puedo confirmar ni desmentir and no es que…, es que…

lessons.title: Weigh it up
lessons.goal: Give a balanced, carefully hedged opinion and report what others say with some distance.

culture.title: Ahorita y otros matices
culture.body: How direct you can be varies across the Spanish-speaking world. In Spain, a plain Ponme un café at a bar counter is normal rather than rude, and disagreement is often voiced quite openly. In Mexico, people tend to soften requests and refusals much more, with diminutives (un cafecito) and polite questions such as ¿Me podría…?, and a blunt no can sound harsh. The famous Mexican ahorita literally means "right now", but depending on the context it can mean in a moment, later or even, very politely, probably never. Reading these nuances matters as much as getting the grammar right.

phrases.t: Yo no lo vería tan negro.
phrases.n: I wouldn't see it so bleakly.

phrases.t: Habría que verlo con más calma.
phrases.n: We'd need to look at it more carefully.

phrases.t: Al parecer, el ayuntamiento ya lo ha decidido.
phrases.n: Apparently the city council has already decided.
phrases.note: al parecer / por lo visto = apparently: reporting with distance. Latin America often: la alcaldía, el municipio.

phrases.t: Eso sí, no creo que sea la solución definitiva.
phrases.n: Mind you, I don't think it's the final solution.

free.n: Should city centres be closed to cars? Give a balanced, carefully hedged opinion: soften your view, concede a point, express doubt with the subjunctive and report what others say with some distance.
free.hint: Yo diría que … / Hasta cierto punto … / Al parecer … / Es cierto que …; eso sí, … / No creo que + subjunctive / Puede que …
free.model: Yo diría que cerrar el centro a los coches es una buena idea, aunque con matices. Al parecer, en algunas ciudades ha bajado la contaminación, pero no creo que sea la solución para todo el mundo. Es cierto que los peatones lo agradecen; eso sí, habría que pensar en las personas mayores y en quienes viven lejos. Puede que con un buen transporte público funcione mejor. Hasta cierto punto, depende de cada ciudad.
